candidate_relations.rationale: The explicit source-type acceptance and duplicate-locator rejection are concrete entrypoint behaviors that strengthen the broader compatibility-adapter proposition that source selection is explicit rather than inferred.

The bootstrap tests show project/2 identity is created only from explicit identity and legacy migration also requires explicit identity, strengthening the project/2 prohibition on inferring identity from repository or environment state.

The reconciliation tests exercise immutable candidate identity and fail-closed disposition handling, strengthening the runtime proposition that reconciliation validates candidates and persists dispositions under the reconciliation scope.
Requiring a complete explicit v2 identity before legacy configuration migration strengthens the project/2 rule that project identity fields are explicit and not inferred.

The orchestrator contract explicitly places initial operator establishment outside bootstrap, strengthening the project-bootstrap proposition that bootstrap creates no operator or other authority state.

The governance runtime implements operational provenance as content-addressed artifacts with typed reference dispatch, strengthening the operational-provenance contract that provenance is immutable observational context bound to an exact subject.

The Distiller ingestion tests verify deterministic request and activation-bundle creation, stable source identities, and bounded non-interactive evidence expansion, strengthening the ingestion-operation proposition.

The ingestion operation constructs only bounded invocation artifacts and excludes repository metadata, installed state, and project knowledge from evidence selection, strengthening the orchestrator requirement not to silently broaden Distiller evidence.

Mapping grant authority only into bounded role-registry and operator-disable paths strengthens the grant-runtime proposition that operation classes and scope targets are explicit rather than unrestricted.

The grant tests show definitions are immutable and non-delegable operations fail at grant creation, strengthening the bounded grant-operations proposition that grants cannot become generic unrestricted mutation authority.

The grant runtime requires explicit operation classes and scope constraints and rejects unsupported scope fields, strengthening the proposition that grant authority is mapped only into bounded operation paths.

Deterministically deriving the candidate submission ID from invocation identity and canonical graph bytes strengthens the production-invocation contract requirement that submission identity be deterministic for fixed local inputs.

The Human-to-Agent rule that an authority grant cannot waive a required materiality acknowledgement strengthens the broader rule that auto-advance is continuation eligibility rather than a source of authority.
The role runtime explicitly separates role registration from Steward authorization state, strengthening the Steward-authorization contract rule that registration alone never grants a Steward scope.
The Steward-authorization tests verify independent scopes, no automatic default Steward, and scope-local reassignment or revocation, strengthening the authorization contract.

Recognizing both the exact legacy project/1 configuration and the explicit project/2 identity contract strengthens the project-identity amendment as the governed v2 identity representation rather than an inferred replacement.

Prohibiting hard-coded framework reads of project state and requiring project-owned package and workflow inputs strengthens the migration requirement to remove cross-repository runtime coupling while preserving project ownership.

The authorization tests exercise independent scope state and scope-local reassignment and revocation, strengthening the runtime proposition that Steward authorization is maintained as a separate domain.

The workflow contract rule that workflow intent grants no downstream approval, activation, semantic authority, admission authority, or lock strengthens the broader rule that auto-advance is only continuation eligibility.

The shared-orchestration tests exercise grant-derived auto-advance, stale-state stops, materiality pauses, ambiguous grants, and grant consumption boundaries, strengthening the common-mutation distinction between direct-operator and grant-derived approval.

The project-bootstrap contract explicitly excludes operator and other authority creation, strengthening the orchestrator design rule that the first authority-sensitive operation requires a separate initial-operator ceremony.

The Rupi install/bootstrap handoff tests show bootstrap stops at the authority boundary and does not advance failures into authority work, strengthening the orchestrator design rule that authority setup is separate from bootstrap.

The adversarial Rupi tests show administrative language and prior context cannot manufacture operator or Steward authority, strengthening the requirement for an explicit initial-operator ceremony before authority-sensitive work.
